title: Using Experience Twice: Dynamic Process Rubrics for Privileged Token-Level Credit Assignment
title_zh: 双重利用经验：用于特权级词元级信用分配的动态过程评分规则

paragraphs.en: Agent trajectories often contain both successful decisions and failed attempts, yet optimization with sparse trajectory-level rewards struggles to identify which critical decisions should be reinforced or suppressed. We observe that meaningful distinctions among on-policy trajectories can be distilled into natural-language process rubrics and used as process supervision signals. Based on this insight, we propose Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD), which leverages self-derived process rubrics for dense token-level supervision, thereby augmenting outcome-centric reinforcement learning. Specifically, the current policy independently generates multiple rubric bundles at each step according to the same group of trajectories, extracting candidate process rubrics from cross-trajectory behavioral differences. A frozen verifier then evaluates all rubric items against each trajectory in the group, and selects one candidate bundle based on bundle-level alignment between rubric satisfaction and task success. ORSD treats the selected rubric bundle as privileged information during training, then compares the log-likelihoods of the original tokens with and without the rubric. The resulting likelihood gap provides token-specific process credit, which is added to the original trajectory-level GRPO advantage through additive advantage shaping. ORSD thus bridges trajectory-level outcome supervision and fine-grained process supervision, enabling token-level credit assignment using process signals. Extensive experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that ORSD accelerates policy improvement and boosts final task performance for both Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B under the same environment-interaction budget. Our code is available at https://github.com/AnnaXChun/ORSD .
paragraphs.zh: 智能体的轨迹通常既包含成功的决策，也包含失败的尝试，然而基于稀疏的轨迹级奖励进行优化难以识别哪些关键决策应当被强化或抑制。 我们观察到，同策略（on-policy）轨迹之间的有意义差异可以提炼为自然语言的过程准则，并用作过程监督信号。 基于这一洞见，我们提出在线准则自蒸馏（ORSD），它利用自生成的过程准则进行密集的词元级监督，从而增强以结果为中心的强化学习。 具体而言，当前策略根据同一组轨迹，在每一步独立生成多个准则包，从跨轨迹的行为差异中提取候选过程准则。 随后由一个冻结的验证器针对组中的每条轨迹评估所有准则条目，并依据准则满足情况与任务成功之间的包级一致性来选择一个候选包。 ORSD 在训练期间将选定的准则包视为特权信息，然后比较有无该准则时原始词元的对数似然。 由此产生的似然差提供了词元特定的过程信用，并通过加性优势塑形将其叠加到原始的轨迹级 GRPO 优势上。 因此，ORSD 架起了轨迹级结果监督与细粒度过程监督之间的桥梁，能够利用过程信号进行词元级的信用分配。 在 ALFWorld 和 WebShop 上的大量实验表明，在相同的环境交互预算下，ORSD 能够加速策略改进并提升 Qwen3-1.7B 和 Qwen3-4B 的最终任务性能。 我们的代码发布于 https://github.com/AnnaXChun/ORSD 。

paragraphs.en: Large language model (LLM) agents have shown strong capabilities in web interaction ( Zhou et al., 2024a ) and software engineering ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , with applications extending to embodied exploration ( Wang et al., 2024 ) . Yet reliable decision-making in interactive environments remains challenging: agents must plan sequences of actions, explore unfamiliar situations, and reflect on feedback to revise unsuccessful strategies. Recent progress in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) offers a promising training approach. DeepSeek-R1 ( Guo et al., 2025 ) shows that verifiable reward feedback can substantially improve reasoning performance, with reflection and self-verification emerging during reinforcement learning. Building on these advances, agentic RL has also adopted Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) ( Shao et al., 2024 ) to train agents through environment interaction, as demonstrated by RAGEN ( Wang et al., 2025 ) in multi-turn tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）智能体已在网络交互（Zhou et al., 2024a）和软件工程（Yang et al., 2024）中展现出强大的能力，其应用还扩展到了具身探索（Wang et al., 2024）。 然而，在交互环境中进行可靠决策仍然具有挑战性：智能体必须规划动作序列，探索陌生情境，并对反馈进行反思以修正不成功的策略。 近来在可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR）方面的进展提供了一种很有前景的训练方法。 DeepSeek-R1（Guo et al., 2025）表明，可验证的奖励反馈能够显著提升推理性能，反思与自我验证会在强化学习过程中涌现。 基于这些进展，智能体强化学习（agentic RL）也采用了组相对策略优化（GRPO）（Shao et al., 2024），通过与环境交互来训练智能体，正如 RAGEN（Wang et al., 2025）在多轮任务中所展示的那样。

paragraphs.en: Despite these advances, relying solely on outcome rewards provides limited guidance about which intermediate decisions deserve credit. Under trajectory-level GRPO, all policy-generated tokens within a trajectory share the same advantage, so useful actions, redundant steps, and recoverable mistakes receive the same learning signal. To assign credit to individual steps, GiGPO ( Feng et al., 2025 ) groups actions from matching environment states across trajectories and estimates step-level advantages through within-group comparisons. This refines credit across decisions, although tokens within each action still share the same step-level signal. More recently, natural-language rubrics have emerged as another source of supervision by making task-specific evaluation criteria explicit. Rubrics as Rewards ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) use these criteria to construct reward signals. RLCF ( Viswanathan et al., 2025 ) constructs instruction-specific checklists in advance and aggregates criterion-level judgments into a response score, while OpenRubrics ( Liu et al., 2026 ) derives rubrics from existing preference pairs and trains a rubric-guided reward model for preference optimization. Although rubric-based methods introduce richer evaluation criteria, their feedback usually still remains at the trajectory level, leaving credit assignment to specially individual tokens unresolved. Moreover, their rubric construction is separate from the policy’s ongoing learning process, so the criteria are not continually updated by the updated policy.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管有这些进展，仅依赖结果奖励对哪些中间决策值得分配信用所提供的指导仍然有限。 在轨迹级 GRPO 下，同一轨迹内所有由策略生成的 token 共享相同的优势，因此有用的动作、冗余的步骤和可恢复的错误会收到相同的学习信号。 为了将信用分配到单个步骤，GiGPO（Feng 等，2025）将来自不同轨迹中匹配环境状态的动作进行分组，并通过组内比较来估计步骤级优势。 这在各个决策之间细化了信用分配，尽管每个动作内部的 token 仍然共享相同的步骤级信号。 更近期的，自然语言评分标准已成为另一种监督来源，它使特定于任务的评估标准显式化。 Rubrics as Rewards（Gunjal 等，2026）使用这些标准来构建奖励信号。 RLCF（Viswanathan 等，2025）预先构建针对具体指令的检查清单，并将标准层面的判断聚合为响应分数，而 OpenRubrics（Liu 等，2026）从现有的偏好对中导出评分标准，并训练一个由评分标准引导的奖励模型用于偏好优化。 尽管基于评分标准的方法引入了更丰富的评估标准，但其反馈通常仍停留在轨迹层面，未能解决针对特殊单个 token 的信用分配问题。 此外，它们的评分标准构建与策略的持续学习过程是分离的，因此这些标准不会随策略的更新而持续更新。

paragraphs.en: These limitations motivate the use of rubrics as privileged context for finer-grained credit assignment. Our core insight is that comparing the log-probabilities assigned to the same sampled tokens with and without rubrics can turn rubric-based guidance into token-level advantages. Such signals can refine trajectory-level advantages, allowing tokens within the same trajectory to receive different credits. Moreover, as the policy evolves during training, its exploration patterns and failure modes may also change. Generating rubrics online from on-policy trajectories allows them to reflect the policy’s current behavior, capturing task-specific constraints, failure patterns, and successful action sequences that static rubrics may overlook. This enables the credit assignment signal to adapt to the evolving policy rather than relying on fixed, predefined criteria. However, jointly deriving rubrics from on-policy experience and leveraging them as privileged context for token-level credit assignment remains underexplored.

paragraphs.en: In this work, we introduce Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD), a framework that turns on-policy experience into adaptive process supervision for token-level credit assignment. ORSD reuses these trajectories to construct process supervision in three steps. First, conditioned on both task prompt and the group of trajectories, the same policy independently generates multiple rubric bundles, each containing multiple criteria for evaluating intermediate states along the trajectories. Second, ORSD employs a verifier to assess the satisfaction of each rubric criterion on every trajectory, producing a satisfaction profile for each rubric bundle. It then measures the alignment between each satisfaction profile and the outcome rewards, and selects the rubric bundle with the highest correlation as privileged information. Third, ORSD augments the prompt with the selected privileged information and recomputes the token likelihoods of the sampled trajectories. The gap between the original and augmented token likelihoods is then used to compute the token-level advantage. As a result, ORSD transforms a group of on-policy trajectories into token-level credit, requiring neither additional rollouts nor additional environment interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 在本工作中，我们提出在线规则自蒸馏（ORSD），这是一个将同策略经验转化为自适应过程监督、用于 token 级信用分配的框架。 ORSD 复用这些轨迹，通过三个步骤构建过程监督。 首先，以任务提示和轨迹组为条件，同一策略独立生成多个规则包，每个规则包包含用于评估轨迹中间状态的多个准则。 其次，ORSD 使用验证器评估每条轨迹上各规则准则的满足情况，为每个规则包生成一个满足度画像。 随后，它度量每个满足度画像与结果奖励之间的一致性，并选择相关性最高的规则包作为特权信息。 第三，ORSD 将选出的特权信息加入提示中，并重新计算采样轨迹的 token 似然。 原始与增广 token 似然之间的差值随后被用于计算 token 级优势。 由此，ORSD 将一组同策略轨迹转化为 token 级信用，既无需额外的 rollout，也无需额外的环境交互。

paragraphs.en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) uses automatically verified outcomes to train language models. PPO and GRPO are commonly used for policy optimization, with GRPO estimating relative advantages within groups of sampled responses ( Schulman et al., 2017 ; Shao et al., 2024 ) . For LLM agents, training involves multiple rounds of interaction, during which policy’s decisions affect subsequent observations and the final reward. RAGEN examines learning dynamics in multi-turn agent RL, and Agent Lightning provides a framework for training agents from their execution traces ( Wang et al., 2025 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) . The environment interaction also supports additional learning signals. EnvRL uses state transitions for representation learning, while T 2 PO adjusts exploration through uncertainty estimates and turn-level resampling ( Wang et al., 2026d ; Wang et al., 2026a ) .
paragraphs.zh: 可验证奖励强化学习（RLVR）使用自动验证的结果来训练语言模型。 PPO 和 GRPO 常用于策略优化，其中 GRPO 通过在采样响应组内估计相对优势来进行优化（Schulman et al., 2017；Shao et al., 2024）。 对于大语言模型智能体，训练涉及多轮交互，在此过程中策略的决策会影响后续观测和最终奖励。 RAGEN 研究了多轮智能体强化学习中的学习动态，Agent Lightning 则提供了一个从智能体执行轨迹中进行训练的框架（Wang et al., 2025；Luo et al., 2025）。 环境交互还能提供额外的学习信号。 EnvRL 利用状态转移进行表示学习，而 T2PO 则通过不确定性估计和轮次级重采样来调整探索（Wang et al., 2026d；Wang et al., 2026a）。

paragraphs.en: Credit assignment assigns different credit to individual steps or tokens in an agent trajectory. GiGPO groups steps across trajectories by state similarity and estimates relative advantages within each group ( Feng et al., 2025 ) . HGPO further groups steps according to their interaction contexts ( He et al., 2026 ) . ArCHer uses rewards from subsequent interactions to estimate the value of the entire response generated at the current turn, then uses this estimate to update the policy that generates the response ( Zhou et al., 2024b ) . POAD further considers the role of individual tokens within an action: it treats action generation as a sequence of token-level decisions and estimates future rewards for each token, providing a finer-grained training signal ( Wen et al., 2024 ) . SC-GRPO conditions on verified solutions and weights token gradients according to the resulting distributional divergence ( Shan et al., 2026 ) .
paragraphs.zh: 信用分配为智能体轨迹中的各个步骤或词元分配不同的信用。 GiGPO 依据状态相似度对跨轨迹的步骤进行分组，并在每组内估计相对优势（Feng et al., 2025）。 HGPO 进一步根据步骤的交互上下文进行分组（He et al., 2026）。 ArCHer 利用后续交互的奖励来估计当前轮次所生成整个回复的价值，再用该估计值更新生成回复的策略（Zhou et al., 2024b）。 POAD 进一步考虑动作中各个词元的作用：它将动作生成视为词元级决策序列，并为每个词元估计未来奖励，从而提供更细粒度的训练信号（Wen et al., 2024）。 SC-GRPO 以经过验证的解答为条件，并根据由此产生的分布差异对词元梯度进行加权（Shan et al., 2026）。

paragraphs.en: A natural-language rubric is a set of written criteria specifying which aspects of a response or reasoning process to evaluate. Prior work uses rubrics to provide feedback at different levels: Rubrics as Rewards assigns a reward to the entire response based on rubric satisfaction ( Gunjal et al., 2026 ) ; Rubrics to Tokens estimates the relevance of each criterion to individual response tokens, providing token-level feedback ( Xu et al., 2026 ) ; and Step-wise Rubric Rewards checks whether each reasoning step satisfies the criteria and assigns step-level rewards ( Xie et al., 2026 ) . These methods use rubrics to construct fine-grained supervision, with criteria generated offline and held fixed. We further investigate how to generate rubrics online that better match the current policy and use them for token-level credit assignment.
paragraphs.zh: 自然语言量规是一组书面标准，用于明确说明应评估响应或推理过程的哪些方面。 已有工作在不同层级上使用量规来提供反馈：Rubrics as Rewards 依据量规的满足情况为整个响应分配奖励（Gunjal et al., 2026）；Rubrics to Tokens 估计每条标准与响应中各个词元的相关性，从而提供词元级反馈（Xu et al., 2026）；Step-wise Rubric Rewards 检查每个推理步骤是否满足标准并分配步骤级奖励（Xie et al., 2026）。 这些方法使用量规来构建细粒度监督，其标准在离线阶段生成并保持固定。 我们进一步研究如何在线生成能更好匹配当前策略的量规，并将其用于词元级的信用分配。

paragraphs.en: Knowledge distillation trains a student model using teacher predictions, with supervision applied to individual tokens or complete sequences ( Hinton et al., 2015 ; Kim & Rush, 2016 ) . Training can also use data generated by the learner itself: DAgger collects supervision at states visited by the learner’s policy ( Ross et al., 2011 ) , while GKD ( Agarwal et al., 2024 ) trains on student-generated sequences with supervision provided by a teacher. OPSD ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) uses the same model for self-distillation: the model first generates a response, then computes its log-probability given additional information to provide a training signal for the original policy. This additional information is called privileged context. Prior work also extracts such information from task execution records: Skill-SD ( Wang et al., 2026b ) summarizes experience from completed trajectories into natural-language skills, while SDPO ( Hübotter et al., 2026 ) uses environmental feedback and successful attempts for self-distillation.
paragraphs.zh: 知识蒸馏利用教师模型的预测来训练学生模型，监督可以施加在单个词元或完整序列上（Hinton et al., 2015；Kim & Rush, 2016）。 训练还可以使用由学习者自身生成的数据：DAgger 在学习者策略访问过的状态处收集监督信号（Ross et al., 2011），而 GKD（Agarwal et al., 2024）则在学生模型生成的序列上进行训练，监督信号由教师模型提供。 OPSD（Zhao et al., 2026）使用同一个模型进行自蒸馏：模型先生成一个回复，然后在给定附加信息的情况下计算该回复的对数概率，从而为原始策略提供训练信号。 这种附加信息被称为特权上下文。 已有研究还从任务执行记录中提取此类信息：Skill-SD（Wang et al., 2026b）将已完成轨迹的经验总结为自然语言技能，而 SDPO（Hübotter et al., 2026）则利用环境反馈和成功的尝试进行自蒸馏。

paragraphs.en: In this section, we present the proposed Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD), a framework that turns on-policy rollouts into rubrics and then into token-level credit signals. As shown in Figure 1 , at each training step, the current policy first samples a group of trajectories for the same task and obtains a reward for each trajectory. It then generates candidate rubric bundles from the task description and these trajectories. The rubric-reward alignment mechanism selects the bundle whose rubric satisfaction scores correlate most strongly with the rewards across the group. Finally, the token-wise log-likelihood difference between rollouts with and without the selected bundle enables per-token advantage shaping of the original trajectory-level advantage. In this way, ORSD reuses the same on-policy trajectories for rubric generation and privileged paired replay to derive token-specific credit without introducing additional environment interactions.
paragraphs.zh: 在本节中，我们提出所提出的在线评分标准自蒸馏（ORSD）框架，该框架将同策略采样轨迹转化为评分标准，进而转化为词元级别的信用信号。 如图 1 所示，在每个训练步骤中，当前策略首先为同一任务采样一组轨迹，并为每条轨迹获得一个奖励。 然后它根据任务描述和这些轨迹生成候选评分标准包。 评分标准—奖励对齐机制会选出其评分标准满足分数与该组内奖励相关性最强的评分标准包。 最后，有与无所选评分标准包的采样轨迹之间的逐词元对数似然差，可用于对原始轨迹级优势进行逐词元优势塑形。 通过这种方式，ORSD 复用相同的同策略轨迹进行评分标准生成与特权成对重放，从而在无需额外环境交互的情况下推导出词元特定的信用信号。

paragraphs.en: These results demonstrate the effectiveness of ORSD across household interaction and web shopping tasks. Its overall gains extend beyond GRPO to GiGPO and the reported self-distillation baselines, including SDAR. ORSD derives task-specific process criteria from rollout differences and uses the selected rubric to refine token-level learning signals through paired replay. The improvements over GRPO under the same environment-interaction budget support this approach to extracting additional supervision from existing trajectories. The following ablations examine the contributions of online rubric generation and rubric-reward alignment.
paragraphs.zh: 这些结果证明了 ORSD 在家庭交互和网页购物任务上的有效性。 其整体增益不仅扩展到 GRPO 之外，还超越了 GiGPO 以及所报告的自蒸馏基线，包括 SDAR。 ORSD 从 rollout 差异中推导出任务特定的过程评估标准，并利用所选的评分准则通过成对回放来改进 token 级别的学习信号。 在相同的环境交互预算下，相对 GRPO 的提升支持了这种从现有轨迹中提取额外监督的方法。 以下消融实验检验了在线评分准则生成和评分准则-奖励对齐的贡献。

paragraphs.en: To evaluate the effectiveness of online rubric generation, we construct an Offline Rubric variant. Before RL training, the initial policy generates one task-specific rubric bundle for each task, and these rubrics remain fixed throughout training. As shown in Table 2 , Offline Rubric consistently improves over GRPO on both model scales, confirming that task-specific rubric supervision is already beneficial even when generated only once. However, it still falls short of online ORSD by 4.80 percentage points in success rate for both backbones. This gap highlights the value of refreshing the rubric from the current policy’s rollouts, so that the supervision remains aligned with the policy’s changing behavior and failure modes during training. Importantly, both variants generate rubrics automatically and require no manually authored criteria.
paragraphs.zh: 为了评估在线量规生成的有效性，我们构建了一个离线量规（Offline Rubric）变体。 在强化学习训练之前，初始策略为每个任务生成一个特定于任务的量规包，并且这些量规在整个训练过程中保持固定。 如表 2 所示，离线量规在两个模型规模上都稳定优于 GRPO，这表明即使只生成一次，特定于任务的量规监督也已经是有效的。 然而，它在两个骨干模型上的成功率仍比在线 ORSD 低 4.80 个百分点。 这一差距凸显了从当前策略的 rollout 中刷新量规的价值，从而使监督在训练过程中与策略不断变化的行为和失败模式保持一致。 重要的是，两种变体都自动生成量规，且无需人工编写的评估标准。

paragraphs.en: ORSD selects candidate rubric bundles based on their alignment with outcome rewards. We examine this design through two ablations. ORSD w/o Rubric-Reward Alignment generates a single bundle and uses it directly, omitting verifier scoring and candidate selection. Random Rubric retains the same candidate count as full ORSD ( M = 4 M=4 ) but replaces alignment-based selection with random selection. Table 2 shows that full ORSD outperforms both variants on both model scales. Relative to the single-bundle variant, ORSD improves success by 2.15 and 9.45 percentage points on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, respectively. With the candidate count held fixed, alignment-based selection improves success over random selection by 3.40 and 7.15 percentage points, with corresponding score gains of 5.36 and 4.08 points. These consistent gains demonstrate the effectiveness of rubric-reward alignment in selecting process supervision for policy training, with the selected rubrics serving as privileged context for token-level advantage shaping.

paragraphs.en: We introduced Online Rubric Self-Distillation (ORSD) to improve credit assignment in LLM agent reinforcement learning. ORSD generates task-specific process rubrics online from differences among on-policy trajectories, without manually authored or fixed offline criteria. Rubric-reward alignment selects the bundle whose satisfaction scores best correlate with outcomes. Through privileged paired replay, the selected rubric converts token-level likelihood gaps into token-level advantage corrections, providing fine-grained supervision without additional environment interactions. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B show the best overall performance among the compared methods, while ablations validate online rubric generation and candidate selection. These results highlight the value of deriving adaptive process supervision from the policy’s own experience for credit assignment in long-horizon agent tasks.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了在线评分标准自蒸馏（Online Rubric Self-Distillation，ORSD），以改进大语言模型智能体强化学习中的信用分配。 ORSD 在线地从同策略轨迹之间的差异中生成任务特定的过程评分标准，而无需人工撰写或固定的离线标准。 评分标准-奖励对齐会选择其满足度得分与结果最相关的评分标准组合。 通过特权成对回放，被选中的评分标准将词元级似然差距转化为词元级优势修正，从而在无需额外环境交互的情况下提供细粒度监督。 在 ALFWorld 和 WebShop 上使用 Qwen3-1.7B 和 Qwen3-4B 进行的实验表明，我们的方法在所比较的方法中取得了最佳的整体性能，同时消融实验验证了在线评分标准生成与候选选择的有效性。 这些结果凸显了从策略自身经验中推导自适应过程监督对长时程智能体任务信用分配的价值。
